history.period: Founded 1965-1966 with the rest of the GRL monastery complex
history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — keep-or-drop decision needed. This is a Tibetan Buddhist monastery of the Gelugpa (Yellow Hat) tradition. The Middle Gompa is the middle of three sections (Upper, Middle, Lower) of the GRL (Gentse Gaden Rabgyel Lling) Monastery at Bomdila, founded 1965-66 by the 12th reincarnate of Tsona Gontse Rinpoche as a replica of the Tsona Gontse Monastery in South Tibet. The middle and lower sections contain the prayer halls and meditation spaces for the monastic community, and a prominent statue of the Medicine Buddha in the middle gompa historically served as a gathering place for those seeking guidance on healing matters. RELATED ROW: CSV seq 68 (Upper Gompa) is the upper section of the SAME monastery complex — filed separately per instructions.

name: Middle Gompa (Gentse Gaden Rabgyel Lling Monastery)
town_description: Bomdila (elev. ~7,300-8,000 ft) is the headquarters of West Kameng district, a scenic hill town on the Tezpur-Bhalukpong-Tawang route, known for its Buddhist monasteries, panoramic views of the Kangto and Gorichen peaks, and as the main stopover between the plains of Assam and Tawang.

travel.airport: Tezpur airport is the nearest (~175 km, verify); Guwahati (Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi International) is the main gateway (~330 km).
travel.railway: Nearest railheads: Bhalukpong / Tezpur / Guwahati (verify); official West Kameng tourism lists Bhalukpong, Tezpur and Guwahati.
travel.road: On the Tezpur-Bhalukpong-Bomdila-Tawang highway (NH-13); the GRL monastery is a short drive/trek above Bomdila town.

visitor_information.best_time: October to April - pleasant weather, clear views (verify).
visitor_information.opening_hours: Not documented separately from the monastery as a whole; most Arunachal gompas admit daytime visitors, with morning and evening prayers (verify). Dress respectfully; photography may be restricted inside prayer halls.
